checks.finding: AC-038 (requirements.md:909) and its mirror TEST-038 (acceptance-tests.md:84) name three exemplar fixtures -- `lite-check-source-undefined`, `output-schema-validation-failed`, `snapshot-generation-mismatch` -- and then assert, in the parenthetical this round's edit added, that `resolver-evidence.yaml` 'is itself staged at step (j) and **is** written on each of these three fixtures per AC-012'. `output-schema-validation-failed` is not one fixture but two, which AC-055 (requirements.md:926) and TEST-055 (acceptance-tests.md:101) deliberately separate: sub-case (a), where Resolver Evidence itself fails its own defensive self-validation and the invocation 'writes NOTHING to any live path, not even a best-effort, fields-omitted Evidence instance', and sub-case (b), where a non-Evidence artifact fails and Evidence is written. AC-012 (requirements.md:883) names sub-case (a) as one of exactly two exceptions to the always-emitted rule. Sub-case (a) is squarely inside AC-038's own scope, because Evidence is staged at REQ-001 step (j) and validated at step (k) (requirements.md:308-310), so it is a Block 'reached only after this invocation has already staged ... in memory'. DOWNSTREAM FAILURE MODE: the author of TEST-038's fixture cannot decide which `output-schema-validation-failed` sub-case to instantiate; instantiating (a) yields an Evidence-exists assertion that TEST-055(a) and TEST-012 require to be false, and instantiating (b) silently narrows AC-038's stated scope with no text saying so. WHY SPEC REVIEW: both statements are frozen Phase-1 acceptance criteria in requirements.md and acceptance-tests.md, and neither defers the choice to design, task decomposition, or the quality gate; a task author has no authority to narrow an AC. WHY MAJOR: this is the same over-generalisation class the f9cd92ae edit set out to close -- AC-038's own parenthetical says it replaces an unscoped 'artifact' that 'read against AC-012/AC-040/AC-055' -- reintroduced in the replacement wording against AC-055 specifically. It produces a contradictory fixture obligation rather than an unsafe runtime state, so Major rather than Critical. Suggested minimal fix: scope the clause to `output-schema-validation-failed`'s non-Evidence sub-case (AC-055(b)), as AC-055 already words it.

The predicate that replaced the step list is internally self-contradictory in the one site every other site now delegates to. requirements.md:332-340 (REQ-001 step (m)) reads: 'on any Block at which no publication artifact is left standing -- every Block in REQ-002's taxonomy OTHER THAN those whose own rollback restores previously-published bytes, and INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO those reached at (0)/(a)/(h)/(i)/(k)/(l)/(m) ... -- the invocation writes **only** Resolver Evidence's own record of that Block ... **That one-member write set is published directly, not through the journaled transaction**'. The only Blocks step (m) can raise are `artifact-publication-failed` and `post-publication-generation-mismatch` (requirements.md:321-323), and those are precisely the Blocks whose rollback restores previously-published bytes (requirements.md:407 'restoring that target's own PRE-transaction live bytes'; :408 'rolls every just-completed rename back to its own PRE-transaction state'). The same sentence therefore excludes and includes the identical two ids. Four sibling sites resolve it against the carve-out: (1) REQ-002's `post-publication-generation-mismatch` row, requirements.md:408 -- '`resolver-evidence.yaml` is never rolled back and instead receives this Block's own record, WRITTEN DIRECTLY after the rollback completes (AC-012)'; (2) REQ-004, requirements.md:616-624 -- states the identical predicate with NO rollback carve-out at all ('any Block at which no publication artifact is left standing, except (k)'s self-referential case') while asserting that step (m) 'carries the same correction'; (3) Security Boundaries, requirements.md:1265-1279 -- 'When Resolver Evidence is a Block's whole write set, that write never passes through the on-disk area ... the two step-(m) Blocks `artifact-publication-failed` and `post-publication-generation-mismatch` reach an Evidence-only write set ... the invariant is about the Evidence write's own ROUTE'; (4) Field Definitions 'Block', requirements.md:961-967. A second, independent defect in the same clause: 'left standing' is undefined with respect to artifacts a PRIOR successful resolve already published, which AC-011 (requirements.md:882) explicitly contemplates surviving a Block ('or is unchanged from its pre-invocation state'). Read literally, on any re-resolve a publication artifact IS left standing at every Block, so the predicate would select no Block at all and the direct-write route would never apply -- contradicting AC-047 (requirements.md:918), which requires Evidence 'written directly per REQ-001 step (m)' on `publication-journal-recovery`. DOWNSTREAM FAILURE MODE: a Phase-2 implementer and the TEST-039/TEST-047/TEST-049 fixture author cannot decide whether Evidence for the two step-(m) ids travels the direct `temp file + fsync + rename` or the journaled transaction; no acceptance criterion pins it (AC-039 and AC-049 assert only that the record exists and that publication artifacts are rolled back; AC-047 pins the route for `publication-journal-recovery` alone). Taking the carve-out at face value routes the `artifact-publication-failed` Evidence write through the very transaction whose write/fsync/rename has just failed, so AC-012's always-emitted rule can go unsatisfied on the one Block whose whole purpose is to record that the publication failed -- the fail-closed audit obligation requirements.md:371-373 says REQ-004 exists to guarantee. WHY SPEC REVIEW: the conflict is between frozen Phase-1 statements (REQ-001 step (m) vs REQ-002's own diagnostic row, REQ-004, Security Boundaries, Field Definitions); no later gate can choose between two normative requirement sentences. WHY CRITICAL: a direct conflict on a fail-closed publication/audit workflow boundary, located in the single normative 'rollback-and-no-write scope rule' that this round's edit made fifteen other sites point at, so the wrong resolution propagates everywhere at once. Suggested minimal fix: delete the 'other than those whose own rollback restores previously-published bytes' clause (REQ-004 already states the predicate without it) and define 'left standing' as 'left standing by this invocation's own publication transaction', so the predicate is stable across first-resolve and re-resolve.

Material negative, empty, boundary and failure paths implied by the requirements each carry an independently-triggerable acceptance test. All sixteen REQ-002 diagnostic ids have one fixture each plus a clean negative proving no diagnostic fires (AC-010/TEST-010, acceptance-tests.md:59). Empty state: zero affected components is specified as a legitimate non-Block resolution with `trigger_evaluations[]: []` and is fixtured separately from the general one-per-component rule (Edge Cases requirements.md:1107-1126; AC-018/TEST-018). Boundary/race states: pre-publication TOCTOU on digests and on the `affected_components` set difference alone (AC-040/AC-048), the post-recheck race after every rename has briefly succeeded (AC-049), the mid-pipeline step-(e) Registry re-read site (AC-057), and both crash-recovery branches -- convergeable and unconvergeable (AC-047). Failure modes of the fix's own edges: `output-schema-validation-failed` gets both sub-cases (AC-055), `diagnostics[]` gets the multi-node warn cardinality plus the evaluation-abort exception with a named fixture (AC-056), and the fail-closed absent-component case gets its own fixture asserting the Block fires before any predicate evaluation (AC-058). Re-resolve over pre-existing files is covered by AC-011/TEST-011's 'or, if a pre-existing file was present before the run, is byte-unchanged'. Reader-side and provenance negatives are covered (AC-050/AC-051/AC-054). The one state with no automated fixture, `required-present-empty`, is disclosed with a structural reason -- Epic A2's `lite_policy` schema is `additionalProperties: false` so no conforming Registry can express the key, and a synthetic extension would fail `validate-capability-registry` (TEST-009, acceptance-tests.md:58) -- which is a documented impossibility, not a silent gap. The AC-038 sub-case defect is recorded under AMBIGUITY rather than here, because the fixture exists and the defect is in which sub-case it names.

Every assumption is either resolved by investigation or carries an explicit, owned pre-design/pre-implementation action. The three Assumptions (requirements.md:1329-1352) are each paired with a named fallback: sibling A1/A2/A3 contract landing (with a stated follow-up-edit obligation mirroring A4's identical assumption, INV-004); the `guard-invariants.json` protected-suffix reservation, with an explicit re-verification-then-choose-sequencing instruction if it is not yet live (INV-003); and the `SKILL.md` unprotected status, explicitly labelled a live-repository snapshot to be re-verified at implementation start (INV-017). Open Questions are disposed of, not deferred silently: OQ-001 and OQ-002 are assigned to a future caller/epic and mirrored in Non-goals (requirements.md:819-821), and OQ-003 is recorded as resolved by INV-020 with a concrete file:line anchor plus a position-sensitive fingerprint check (AC-053/TEST-053) guarding the citation. The one genuine cross-epic gap, INV-019's missing `required_lite_checks` source, is not left as an assumption at all: Dependencies (requirements.md:138-163) names it as an owned prerequisite with owner (Epic A2 maintainers), scope (an additively-versioned field), migration note, and the narrowed blast radius (`required`-enforcement Lite only), and Non-goals (:807-811) states this feature will not add the field. investigation.md's `## Amendment Re-Review Context` (:792-887, extended through :1826-1834) meets the calibration's full evidence bar -- full commit hashes, per-document SHA-256 at each amendment commit, verbatim dated human-approval quotations, and commit or SHA-256 for every later-phase artifact referenced -- so the phase-sequencing suppression applies and I raise no finding whose sole basis is that later-phase artifacts exist or are cited while Spec-Review-Status is Pending.

Three human/governance boundaries are in scope and each is stated as an observable assertion rather than an intention. (1) Protected-path authorship: Roles and Permissions (requirements.md:993-1022) fixes the human-copy staging route for the three scripts' immutable code under `specs/<feature>/human-copy/` for human application via `apply-human-copy`, explicitly scopes that role to code only, and assigns live generated artifacts to the running Resolver process instead -- the M7 correction that removes the incoherent 'human-copy populates a recomputed value' path. AC-026/TEST-026 makes the staging observable (a staged `test.yml` candidate under `human-copy/` with a correct `MANIFEST.sha256` entry) and records the residual human step in its own Status column, 'Status resolves through a human `cp` action for the `test.yml` portion', rather than asserting an agent can complete it. (2) The `plugins/**` no-edit boundary is testable by AC-032/TEST-032 as a `git diff --stat` over this package's own two registration commits, with the result recorded in the Spec-Authoring-Time Manual Review Record (acceptance-tests.md:130-133). (3) The irreversible-change boundary -- publishing live artifacts -- is governed by the journaled transaction and made testable by AC-011, AC-038, AC-039, AC-047, AC-049 and the reader-side AC-054. The frozen-document amendments themselves carry verbatim, dated approval quotations in investigation.md (e.g. rulings D(1)/D(2) at :1361-1419), so the governance trail for the amendment is citable rather than asserted. Note that the CONTRADICTION finding above bears on WHICH write route applies at two Blocks, not on whether an approval boundary is testable, so it is scored there and not here.

The package hands implementation-policy review a complete product-behaviour surface: an exact CLI shape with a stated no-inference rule for `--feature` (REQ-001, requirements.md:231-248); a thirteen-step processing order with the staged-generation invariant stated as structural rather than a per-step promise; a closed sixteen-row Block taxonomy with a per-row trigger condition and a stated no-fail-open property (REQ-002); a fixed exit-code contract (AC-013) and a fixed diagnostic-line grammar with a determinism-preserving no-verbatim-stderr rule (AC-014, REQ-005); output shapes delegated field-by-field to Epic A4's already-frozen schemas plus one new schema whose fields, cardinalities, bidirectional-consistency and uniqueness rules are all fixed at requirement level (REQ-004); a determinism scope that names its own exceptions explicitly (REQ-003's `state` plus two enforcement-derived digests, and the single `lite-check-source-undefined` divergence); and a caller contract with a concrete file:line insertion anchor plus a position-sensitive drift check (REQ-007, AC-053). A design reviewer is not asked to invent missing product behaviour. The two FAILs above are localized textual conflicts in which a determinate majority reading exists (four sites against one clause for CONTRADICTION; AC-055's own sub-case split for AMBIGUITY), so they are remediation items rather than readiness blockers. NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATION, deliberately not scored as a finding: this round's precheck `edit_summary` ends 'Commit d0f2f0a records the remediation in investigation.md with per-document SHA-256 for all six changed documents.' No such hash appears anywhere in investigation.md, and neither does the replacement value supplied at launch; the calibration-conforming record names `f9cd92aea58e76308e96c0455cef3ab2f57a50b0` (documents only) at investigation.md:1786-1787 and carries the six per-document SHA-256 values at :1826-1834. The precheck's load-bearing fields -- `requirements_sha256`, `acceptance_sha256`, `calibration_sha256` -- all match my manifest, so no check turns on the erroneous value. I record rather than raise it because precheck-result.json is a gate artifact, not a Phase-1 specification artifact, and the calibration's Finding Evidence Gate requires a requirement, acceptance criterion, non-goal, constraint, or investigation claim as the basis of a FAIL.

Check recorded as skipped: the target project has no `domain/` directory, so there is no `domain/context-map.md` carrying `Domain-Model-Status: Approved` and no `domain/domain-contract.json` to validate against. A repository-root probe for `domain/*` returned no entries, and no `domain/` path appears in the allowed-input manifest. With no approved domain model there is no `Bounded-Context:` relation to verify and no canonical-term/`forbidden_synonyms` vocabulary against which to test acceptance-tests.md, so the check's explicit skip condition is met.
